passage.title: Library opening hours announcement
passage.transcript: Hello everyone. Starting next week, the community library will stay open until eight in the evening on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We are making this change because many students and workers asked for more time to study after school and work. All other opening hours will remain the same.

learning_path_questions.prompt: [MOCK 003] What change is the speaker mainly describing?

options.text: The library will close on weekdays.
The library is moving to a new building.
The community library will open later on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The speaker is announcing a new language course.

learning_path_questions.explanation: The announcement focuses on extending the library's evening hours on two days. (Câu mẫu được sinh tự động để kiểm thử giao diện và luồng dữ liệu.)

passage.title: Saturday workshop details
passage.transcript: A reminder about Saturday's writing workshop: it begins at nine thirty in the morning in Room 204. Please bring a notebook and arrive ten minutes early. If you have not registered yet, complete the online form before Friday evening.

learning_path_questions.prompt: [MOCK 002] Which room should participants go to?

options.text: The workshop begins at 8:30 a.m. on Sunday.
The workshop begins at 2:00 p.m. on Friday.
The workshop begins at 9:30 a.m. on Saturday.
The workshop begins at 10:30 a.m. on Monday.

learning_path_questions.explanation: The speaker directly states that the workshop begins at nine thirty on Saturday morning. (Câu mẫu được sinh tự động để kiểm thử giao diện và luồng dữ liệu.)

passage.title: A shared neighborhood garden
passage.text: Last spring, residents turned an unused corner beside their apartment building into a shared garden. Families now grow vegetables, children learn about plants, and neighbors meet while watering the beds. The garden has not solved every problem in the area, but it has made the space greener and helped residents feel more connected.

learning_path_questions.prompt: [MOCK 002] Which title best summarizes the text?

options.text: Residents are planning to move to a different apartment building.
The city has banned families from growing vegetables.
A shared garden has improved a local space and brought neighbors together.
The passage explains how to build a large shopping center.

learning_path_questions.explanation: The passage describes the garden's benefits for the neighborhood and its residents. (Câu mẫu được sinh tự động để kiểm thử giao diện và luồng dữ liệu.)

question_pool_passages.title: Focusing on Our Gallery Opening

question_pool_passages.title: Convenience at Corner Market

question_pool_passages.title: Protecting Our Shoreline

Because we limit group sizes to twelve people, we can ensure everyone learns about local wildlife without disturbing the nesting birds. If you follow these simple guidelines, you will help us maintain this natural paradise for years to come. We truly appreciate your cooperation in keeping our coastline wild and clean.

question_pool_passages.title: Updates to Summer Swim Lessons
question_pool_passages.transcript: Hello everyone. I am calling to share some important changes for our community pool swim lessons. question_pool_passages.title: Greening Oak Street
question_pool_passages.transcript: I am so excited that our neighborhood finally agreed to start the street-tree project on Saturday. question_pool_passages.title: A Change of Venue for the Orchestra
question_pool_passages.transcript: Hi everyone, I am calling to update you on our upcoming rehearsal. question_pool_passages.title: Town Hall: The Riverside Project
question_pool_passages.transcript: Good evening, everyone. Thank you for joining this town hall. We are here to discuss the proposed Riverside Park project. We have two main options: a modern playground for children or a quiet walking trail for seniors. Because the old school building was demolished last May, we now have enough empty land to build the trail, but the city council prefers the playground due to the high number of young families moving here. I am personally excited about the potential for a community garden alongside the trail, which would be a wonderful place to relax. Please look at the maps on the wall and leave your written feedback in the box by the door. We really need your input before we make a final decision next month. Your voice matters in shaping our future.

question_pool_passages.title: A Safer Way to School
question_pool_passages.text: As a parent living on Oak Street, I am concerned about the traffic near Elm Primary School. Currently, children must cross the busy road at the intersection of Oak and Main, where cars often drive too fast. While there is a stop sign at Pine Street and a traffic light at Maple Avenue, the crossing at Oak and Main has no safety measures. I propose that we install a pedestrian island in the middle of the road. This would allow students to cross halfway, wait safely, and then finish their journey. Since the current lack of protection makes walking to school dangerous, this small change would significantly improve safety for our children. It is a modest solution that would not require expensive traffic lights, keeping the project cost-effective. I believe that providing a designated space for students is a practical necessity for our neighborhood.

question_pool_passages.title: Sharing for a Better Building
question_pool_passages.text: Living in an apartment building often feels lonely, but creating a tool-sharing library can change that. Instead of every resident buying their own drill, ladder, or vacuum, we should start a communal shelf in the storage room. It is a modest proposal that saves money and reduces clutter in our small homes. For instance, while some neighbors might suggest hiring a professional for all repairs, many minor tasks simply require a basic tool that sits unused in a closet for months. Because we share these items, we create more space in our apartments and strengthen our community bonds. If we cooperate, we can manage our resources more efficiently. While a large, expensive power saw might be too dangerous to share, simple items like hammers and screwdrivers are perfect for this program. By working together, we turn a collection of private units into a real neighborhood where people actually help one another.

question_pool_passages.title: The Community Book Exchange
question_pool_passages.text: Welcome to our new Community Book Exchange, located in the park near the fountain. Our goal is to encourage reading by making books accessible to everyone in the neighborhood. The process is simple: if you take a book, please leave one behind. We kindly ask that you only donate books in good condition, as damaged items create clutter rather than value. While we appreciate all genres, we currently have a surplus of cookbooks, so please try to bring fiction or travel guides instead. This exchange functions on a trust-based system; because we have no staff to monitor the shelves, we rely on residents to keep the area tidy. We believe that sharing stories strengthens our community, even if we only exchange one book at a time. It is a modest way to connect with neighbors while enjoying literature without any cost. Please visit us between 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM daily to find your next great read.

question_pool_passages.title: Greenwood Park Update
question_pool_passages.text: Dear neighbors, I am writing to share our progress on the Greenwood Park renovation. Last month, we installed ten new wooden benches near the pond and planted twenty oak trees along the north fence. While some residents requested a large swimming pool, the committee decided against it. We believe that focusing on quiet spaces is a more sensible approach because our limited budget prevents us from maintaining expensive water facilities. By prioritizing these smaller upgrades, we ensure the park remains a peaceful retreat for everyone rather than a noisy recreational hub. We have also added three new trash bins to keep the area clean. We hope these improvements make your daily walks more pleasant. Please remember that we are working to preserve the natural beauty of our local environment. We welcome your feedback on these changes as we continue to improve our shared space.

question_pool_passages.title: My Kitchen Journey
question_pool_passages.text: Moving into my first apartment was exciting, but learning to cook independently has been a humbling experience. At first, I thought I could master gourmet recipes within a month. However, I soon realized that simple meals are much more practical for a busy student. I started by learning to boil pasta, then mastered scrambled eggs, and finally attempted a stir-fry last Tuesday. While my friends spend hours preparing fancy roasts, I prefer quick dinners because they save me time for my studies. I have also learned that I am a novice in the kitchen; I still burn toast occasionally, even though I have improved at seasoning my vegetables. Cooking requires patience, and although I am not a professional chef, I have become quite resourceful with the few ingredients I keep in my pantry. It is not about making perfect food, but about becoming self-sufficient in my daily life.

question_pool_passages.title: New Flexible Start Times
question_pool_passages.text: Hi team, I am writing to announce that our office is moving to a flexible start time policy starting next Monday. While I believe we must maintain some core hours, I propose allowing employees to arrive between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM. This change is necessary because many of you face heavy traffic during the morning commute, and a staggered schedule will help everyone avoid the stress of rush hour. Unlike our previous policy, which required everyone to be at their desks by 8:30 AM sharp, this new approach should improve our daily productivity. We are also introducing a mandatory team meeting at 11:00 AM every day to ensure we stay connected. Please remember that this is a pilot program for the next three months. If this arrangement proves successful, we will keep it permanently. I am optimistic that this adjustment will create a better work-life balance for everyone, as it gives you more control over your morning routine while still keeping our team goals in focus.

question_pool_passages.title: A New Spot for Your Bike
question_pool_passages.text: The city recently opened a new bicycle parking area near the Central Library, replacing the old, crowded racks that were behind the bus station. I visited it yesterday to see if it lives up to the hype. The new space is quite convenient because it is located directly next to the library entrance, whereas the old ones required a five-minute walk through the park. It features sixty secure metal lockers and space for forty standard bikes. While the design is modern, I noticed that the roof only covers half of the facility, meaning some bikes might get wet during heavy rain. Overall, the new location is a significant improvement for commuters, though the partial shelter is a bit of a shortcoming. It is a practical addition to our city, but I hope they consider extending the roof in the future to keep all bikes protected from the weather.

question_pool_passages.title: Two Paths to Less Waste
question_pool_passages.text: Many households want to reduce food waste, but they often struggle to choose the best method. Two popular approaches are meal planning and composting. Meal planning involves deciding your weekly menu before shopping, which prevents buying extra items you might not finish. It is proactive and stops waste before it starts. On the other hand, composting turns food scraps like peels or cores into soil for gardens. While composting is helpful, it happens after the food is already discarded. Meal planning is generally more effective because it addresses the root cause of waste: over-purchasing. Composting is a great secondary step, but planning ensures that less food enters the bin in the first place. By being mindful at the grocery store, families can save money and help the environment simultaneously. Although composting is a virtuous habit, meal planning is a more direct way to manage what we buy and consume daily.

question_pool_passages.title: Finding Your Perfect Read at the City Library
question_pool_passages.text: Many visitors feel overwhelmed when they enter our library because there are thousands of books on the shelves. If you are a new reader, my modest advice is to start with a genre you already enjoy in movies or TV shows. For example, if you like mystery films, look for a detective novel. This approach is better than choosing a bestseller because you are more likely to finish a book that matches your personal interests. Last year, our library added 500 new classic novels, 200 non-fiction biographies, and 300 mystery thrillers to our collection. While the classics are important, they can be difficult for beginners. By picking a familiar theme, reading becomes an enjoyable habit rather than a chore. It is better to choose a book that feels 'approachable' rather than one that is too complex or long. Once you feel comfortable, you can start exploring different topics or authors. Remember, the best book for you is simply the one that keeps you turning pages until the very end.

question_pool_passages.title: Supporting Our Local Farmers' Market
question_pool_passages.text: Dear City Council, I am writing to express my strong support for the proposed weekly farmers' market in Oak Park. Currently, our town relies heavily on large supermarkets that ship produce from thousands of miles away. By hosting local farmers every Saturday, we can reduce our carbon footprint significantly. While some residents worry about limited parking, the market actually requires less space than the proposed new shopping mall expansion. Furthermore, the market will serve as a hub for our community, allowing neighbors to connect while buying fresh, seasonal food. This initiative is a sustainable choice that benefits our local economy more than the current reliance on distant imports. I believe this market is a sensible way to improve our town's quality of life. I hope you will approve this plan, as it encourages healthier eating habits and strengthens our social bonds. It is time we prioritize our local growers over convenience stores.

question_pool_passages.title: A Change of Plans
question_pool_passages.text: My trip to Lyon was supposed to be simple. I booked the 9:00 AM train from Paris, expecting to arrive by noon. However, a sudden signal failure delayed my departure by three hours. While I was frustrated initially, the extra time gave me a chance to rethink my itinerary. Instead of rushing to the museum as I had planned, I decided to visit a quiet café near the station to write in my journal. Because I was no longer in a hurry, I enjoyed a long lunch and even found a local market I would have otherwise missed. I believe that being flexible is better than sticking to a rigid schedule when things go wrong. Travel is often about the unexpected moments, not just the destinations we aim to reach. By the time I finally boarded, I felt much more relaxed. Sometimes, an inconvenience actually improves the overall quality of a journey because it forces you to slow down and explore your immediate surroundings in a new way.

question_pool_passages.title: Peer Tutoring: Helping Each Other Succeed
question_pool_passages.text: Welcome to our new Peer Tutoring Project! This term, we are pairing older students with younger ones to help with schoolwork. While some teachers think traditional after-school clubs are more effective, I believe peer tutoring is better because students often feel more comfortable asking questions to someone their own age. For example, Sarah in Year 11 helps Mark in Year 7 with his math homework every Tuesday, while David from Year 10 assists Lily in Year 8 with science on Thursdays. Because the older students recently finished these same classes, they understand exactly which topics are confusing. This shared experience makes the tutoring sessions very productive. We hope this initiative becomes a permanent fixture, as it builds confidence and strengthens our school community. If you are struggling with a subject, please sign up in the library by Friday. Join us and let’s grow together!

question_pool_passages.title: Update: Wednesday Community Painting Class
question_pool_passages.text: Dear neighbors, I am writing to share a change to our weekly painting class. We look forward to seeing your creativity at the new location next week. Best regards, Sarah, Class Organizer.

question_pool_passages.title: New Life for the Grand Plaza
question_pool_passages.text: The Grand Plaza, our town’s oldest cinema, is finally reopening this Saturday. However, I believe that saving our history is more valuable than adding a few parking spaces. Unlike the cold, modern shopping centers on the edge of town, the Grand Plaza offers a unique community atmosphere. Because the volunteers prioritized repairing the projector instead of installing a digital snack bar, we can enjoy classic films exactly as they were meant to be seen. While it is true that we need more parking, a town without its cultural landmarks is a town without a soul. This renovation is a modest but important step in keeping our local heritage alive for future generations.

question_pool_passages.title: Running for a Cause
question_pool_passages.text: Last Saturday, I helped organize the 'City Charity Run.' We expected two hundred people, but four hundred runners arrived, which made managing the event quite difficult. Some people think organizing an event is about being in charge, but I believe it is actually about supporting others. question_pool_passages.title: Weekend Discovery: The History Hunt
question_pool_passages.text: Join us this Saturday at the City Museum for our new 'History Hunt' family event. While we know many families enjoy our paid guided tours, we believe that children learn best when they explore at their own pace. Because the tasks are designed for ages 7 to 12, parents can relax while their children engage with historical artifacts. You do not need to book a ticket in advance, but please arrive before 2:00 PM to ensure you have enough time to finish the hunt. We find that this flexible format creates a more relaxed atmosphere for visitors than our traditional, structured afternoon lectures.

question_pool_passages.title: A Fresh Start at The Daily Grind
question_pool_passages.text: Last week, The Daily Grind finally launched their new 'Quick-Pick' breakfast counter. I think the cafe is making a sensible effort to improve speed, but they still need to balance convenience with quality. Their decision to prioritize efficiency is understandable, as the morning crowd is consistently larger than the afternoon rush. question_pool_passages.title: Community Garden Water Initiative
question_pool_passages.text: Attention all Community Garden members. We are starting a new project to collect rainwater for our plants. Starting next Monday, we will install five large blue barrels near the tool shed. While we have a city water supply, using rainwater is more sustainable because it is free and contains no chlorine, which helps our vegetables grow stronger. Please remember that this water is only for the garden plots, not for drinking. To keep the area safe, please ensure the lids are always secure after filling your watering cans. We believe that small changes like this make our community more self-sufficient. We ask that you do not move the barrels, as they are positioned to catch the most runoff from the roof. By using this natural resource, we can reduce our overall water bill and keep our garden healthy throughout the summer. Thank you for helping us make our garden more eco-friendly. Please contact the committee if you have any questions or suggestions about this new system.

question_pool_passages.title: Smartphones in Study Groups: A Balanced View
question_pool_passages.text: Many students argue about whether phones belong in study groups. Some say they are a distraction, while others claim they are essential tools. In my opinion, phones are helpful if we use them with clear boundaries. Last Tuesday, our group spent two hours preparing for our upcoming exams. We used our laptops for history research, but we kept our phones on the table for quick tasks. For instance, we used a calculator app to solve math problems, and we checked the class schedule for our upcoming quiz. However, we agreed to turn off notifications so we would not lose focus. Because we limited our phone use, we finished our work faster than when we were distracted by constant alerts. I believe phones are not inherently bad; they are effective aids as long as the group maintains discipline. If we treat them as tools rather than toys, they definitely improve our collaboration. It is all about setting smart rules before we start working together.

question_pool_passages.title: Fixing the Future at the Oakwood Repair Cafe
question_pool_passages.text: Every third Saturday, the Oakwood Community Center transforms into a bustling Repair Cafe. Instead of throwing away broken items, neighbors bring their damaged belongings to skilled volunteers who help them fix things for free. You might see someone mending a torn jacket, while another person repairs a wobbly wooden chair. Last month, the cafe saved 45 items from the landfill, compared to only 30 items in July. This growth shows that locals are choosing to be more sustainable. I believe this project is a modest but essential step toward a greener town. By learning to mend our possessions, we reduce waste and save money. The atmosphere is always collaborative, as people share tools and knowledge rather than just buying replacements. While we cannot fix every single broken object, the cafe proves that a little effort can significantly extend the life of our belongings. It is a practical way to build community while protecting our environment.

question_pool_passages.title: Choosing the Best Route for the Music Festival
question_pool_passages.text: Hi Sam, I’ve been looking at how to get to the Music Festival this Saturday. We have two main options. The first is the direct train from Central Station. It takes 90 minutes and costs $25. It is definitely the most convenient choice because it drops us right at the main gate. However, the second option is the express bus from the North Terminal. That takes 120 minutes and costs $15. While the train is faster, the bus is cheaper and offers a more scenic route through the countryside. Given that we are on a budget, I think the bus is a sensible choice, even if it adds half an hour to our travel time. I would rather save the ten dollars for extra food at the event. What do you think about taking the slower route to keep our spending down?

question_pool_passages.title: A Friendly Hello Next Door
question_pool_passages.text: Moving to a new place can feel lonely, so I believe welcoming new neighbors is a simple but vital act. Last month, when the Miller family moved into the blue house, I decided to take them a small basket of local fruit. I chose fruit because it is healthier than baked goods, which many people might be allergic to. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, preferred to send a handwritten note, while Mr. Henderson gave them a potted plant. By offering a small gesture, we help newcomers feel at home quickly. It is not about spending a lot of money; it is about building a friendly community. When we show kindness, people usually feel more comfortable in their new environment. Because we take the time to introduce ourselves, the neighborhood becomes a safer and happier place to live. It is a modest way to ensure that everyone feels like they belong here, rather than feeling like outsiders in their own street.

question_pool_passages.title: Inclusive Learning at Oakwood Community Center
question_pool_passages.text: At Oakwood Community Center, we believe that education should be open to everyone, regardless of physical or cognitive ability. We are excited to announce our new autumn schedule, featuring classes designed to be truly inclusive. While we have offered standard art and computer workshops for years, these new sessions provide extra support, such as sign language interpreters and wheelchair-accessible stations. We believe these modifications are essential because they remove barriers that have historically prevented many neighbors from participating. Some might suggest that specialized equipment is unnecessary, but we find that providing these tools leads to a 40% increase in student engagement compared to standard classroom setups. Our goal is to ensure every resident feels welcome. Please note that while our morning yoga starts at 9:00 AM and the evening coding class at 6:00 PM, the inclusive pottery sessions begin promptly at 2:00 PM. We hope these adjustments foster a more equitable environment for all. We encourage you to sign up soon, as space is limited for these popular sessions.

question_pool_passages.title: Green School Competition Report
question_pool_passages.text: Last month, our school organized a recycling competition to encourage greener habits. Students from different grades collected waste to see who could save the most materials. The final results show that Year 10 students collected 45 kilograms of plastic and five kilograms of metal and cardboard, while Year 9 students gathered 38 kilograms of paper and Year 11 students brought 52 kilograms of glass. Because 52 kilograms was the highest team total, the Year 11 team won the top prize. However, I believe the Year 10 team was the most impressive. Although they collected less total weight than Year 11, they gathered a wider variety of materials, including metal and cardboard. This variety shows they worked harder to sort through different types of household items. While the competition was a fun way to learn, our school should focus more on reducing waste rather than just recycling it. Promoting the reuse of bottles and containers would be a more sustainable approach than simply collecting bins of trash at the end of the term. This initiative is a great start, but we must improve our long-term strategy for the future.

question_pool_passages.title: A Request for Comfort
question_pool_passages.text: Dear City Council, I am writing to suggest an improvement for the bus stop on Oak Street. As a daily commuter, I have noticed that the current shelter provides very little protection from the sun during the afternoon. Between 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM, the sun shines directly into the shelter, and the small glass roof fails to block the intense light. Because the roof is transparent, the area underneath becomes uncomfortably hot, making it difficult for elderly passengers to wait safely. Adding a simple opaque cover or a side panel would provide the necessary shade to keep the area cool. While I understand that budgets are limited, this minor adjustment would significantly improve the experience for the many residents who rely on this stop. I believe a more comfortable environment encourages more people to use public transport, which is a positive goal for our town. Thank you for considering this request to make our daily commute a bit better for everyone involved.

question_pool_passages.title: Creative Spaces: The Collective Studio
question_pool_passages.text: In the heart of the city, four local artists have started sharing a single studio space. While some people prefer working alone, this group believes that sharing a workspace is more productive. They split the monthly rent, which saves each person money, and they often exchange feedback on their projects. Sara, a painter, focuses on landscapes, while Mark creates metal sculptures. Because they work in such close proximity, they can easily offer suggestions to improve each other’s drafts. Although they sometimes have different ideas about the best time to clean the room, the benefits of the arrangement clearly outweigh these minor issues. The artists find that being around other creative minds keeps their motivation high. Working together helps them stay focused on their goals. By pooling their resources, they have created a supportive environment that helps them grow as professionals. They prove that collaboration is often better than isolation for developing new artistic skills.

question_pool_passages.title: A Week at the River
question_pool_passages.text: Hi everyone! I just finished my third week volunteering at the River Wildlife Project. We spend most mornings checking the bird nesting boxes, though we also spend time cleaning the riverbank of plastic waste. While the project is making progress, I think we have a long way to go. Last Monday, we counted twelve rare kingfishers, but we only found four active nests, which is fewer than we saw during the same week last year. Because the water level has dropped significantly due to the lack of rain, many fish have moved downstream, making it harder for the birds to find food. This is why we need to continue our efforts to protect the local environment. Our small team is dedicated to restoring this habitat, but we are just one group among many. I feel that our work is helpful, but we should be realistic about how much we can change on our own. We aren't saving the whole river, but we are certainly making a noticeable difference for the wildlife nearby.

question_pool_passages.title: Making Town Meetings Better for Everyone
question_pool_passages.text: Local town meetings are essential for democracy, but they are often hard to attend. Many meetings happen on Tuesday evenings at 7:00 PM, which is difficult for parents and shift workers. As a result, participation is often low. Some towns have started using online streaming, which is a great start. However, we should also consider holding meetings at different times, such as Saturday mornings. If we change the schedule, more residents could participate in local decisions. Another option is providing childcare during the meeting. When citizens can easily access these sessions, the community becomes stronger. I believe that making these small adjustments is a pragmatic way to increase involvement. By removing these barriers, we encourage more people to share their voices. It is time for town councils to prioritize accessibility over tradition, ensuring that every resident has a fair chance to contribute their ideas to the local government.

question_pool_passages.title: A Gentle Walk at Pine Ridge
question_pool_passages.text: If you are looking for a relaxing weekend activity, the Pine Ridge trail is an excellent choice for beginners. Unlike the steep and challenging Mountain Peak route, Pine Ridge is mostly flat, making it accessible for families. I recently visited on a sunny Saturday. While the trail is only three kilometers long, it offers beautiful views of the valley. The path is well-maintained, which is important because the terrain can get muddy after rain. Because of the clear signs along the way, hikers rarely get lost. I believe this trail is the perfect introduction to nature. It is not a place for serious athletes seeking a workout, but it is ideal for those who want a peaceful walk. The path is quite manageable for anyone who can walk comfortably for an hour. Overall, it is a lovely way to spend a few hours without needing any expensive equipment or special training.

question_pool_passages.title: Community Notes: Our Summer Concert Success
question_pool_passages.text: Last Saturday, our town held its annual 'Melody in the Park' event. While professionals usually headline such festivals, this year featured local amateurs, including the high school jazz band and the senior choir. I believe this change was a modest success. Although the sound quality was occasionally uneven, the performance felt more authentic because the musicians were our own neighbors. The jazz band played for forty minutes, followed by the senior choir, who performed for exactly thirty minutes before the evening rain began. Because the performers were local residents, the audience felt a deeper personal connection to the music than in previous years. It was not a perfect show, but it helped us build stronger local bonds. We should continue to support these grassroots efforts, even if they lack the polish of professional tours. Next time, I hope we can organize better microphones to improve the audio clarity for everyone involved.
